I appreciate you sharing that, but I'm not going to change my view just because I'm in the minority. Popularity isn't evidence — plenty of widely-held views have been wrong. The research on attention fragmentation and polarization is real, even if the people you've talked to don't emphasize it.

That said, I'd genuinely enjoy hearing why they see it as net positive. Connection across distance, communities for marginalized people, rapid information sharing — those are real benefits. My position is a judgment about the overall balance, not a denial of the good parts. If you have a strong argument, I'm open to it. I just won't defer to the majority as a shortcut.
